title: A Matching Stand for a Sony XBR
pageTitle: A Matching Stand for a Sony XBR | Mitchell Vizensky
description: A 1995 Sony KV-32XBR45 is 157 pounds of curved black Trinitron, and the stand Sony made for it is long gone. I designed and built a replacement out of plywood that follows the TV's own lines, so the set looks like it shipped that way.

modules.html:
The problem

The XBR45's cabinet isn't a box. The front bows outward and the sides taper toward the back, and Sony sold a matching pedestal to carry those lines down to the floor. Without it, the set sat on whatever furniture was nearby and looked like a TV parked on a table. It also needed something that could hold 157 pounds safely and roll for service.

Designing from the TV itself

  • Trace, don't guess: I took the footprint and the front curve straight from the TV's base, so the top of the stand meets the cabinet edge for edge.
  • Same taper: the sides angle back to match the cabinet, so from any angle the two read as one object.
  • Open front: a deep cubby for consoles and a VCR, wide enough to reach behind for cables.
  • Built for weight: a plywood box with a full top and bottom, on locking casters.

modules.html:
Finishing to match

Plywood edges and a curved front don't look like molded plastic on their own. I filled and sanded every edge into a continuous curve, then finished the whole stand in a textured matte black close to Sony's cabinet, so the seam between TV and stand disappears.

modules.html: It's the same habit I bring to UX work: start from what's already there, match the system instead of fighting it, and finish the details people only notice when they're wrong. More of my restored TVs are on Sunthar.
